verdicts.rewritten_summary: UK Home Office country policy and information note on Russia, SOGI (June 2025): same-sex sexual activity is not criminalised, but same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned, gender-marker changes on documents are prohibited, and trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023; the 2013 'gay propaganda' law is punishable by administrative fines (up to 400,000 rubles for individuals) or detention of up to 15 days, with repeated offences escalating to criminal prosecution and up to four years' imprisonment, and since the November 2023 Supreme Court 'extremist' designation of the international LGBT+ movement, participation carries 2-6 years and organising 6-10 years' imprisonment (Article 282.2). Records at least 139 people in Russia impacted by anti-LGBT+ laws between 2022 and 2024 and assesses that openly LGBT+ people are likely to face discriminatory treatment that, by its nature or repetition, may amount to persecution, the state able but not willing to provide protection. verdicts.rewritten_summary: Human Rights Watch (30 Jun 2025): Russian courts have issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions (about 98 administrative, 3 criminal) for alleged participation in the 'International LGBT Movement' or displaying its symbols since the 2023 Supreme Court 'extremist' designation; between January 2024 and June 2025 at least 20 people faced criminal charges, including three publishing-house staff charged in May 2025 under Article 282.2 who each face up to 12 years' imprisonment, and 81 people were found guilty in 98 administrative cases under Article 20.3 for displaying banned symbols.
